newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Robinsons says bottomline its priority.
newsitem.headline: Robinsons says bottomline its priority.

text.p: Robinson and Co Ltd, one of Singapore's oldest retailers, does not plan to diversify despite a tough trading climate, senior officials said on Thursday.
"We have no plans to diversify outside retail. We want to specialise in retail and don't want to get side-tracked," chairman Michael Wong said at a meeting with the media and analysts.
Wong said the group, which operates its own retail outlets and acts as agent for other chains such as Marks and Spencer, had no immediate plans to expand beyond Singapore and Malaysia.
The group would be opening a new John Little store in Singapore in November, but did not plan to expand its Robinson's department store.
On August 20, Robinson & Co reported a 0.8 percent drop in 1995/1996 net profit to Singapore $25.34 million (US$17.97) on a turnover of S$224.51 million.
According to its 1996 annual report, the group had S$149.72 million in cash and cash equivalent.
Wong said the group was evaluating proposals by various fund managers on how to optimise returns from its cash pile.
"Our returns from retailing are very good...We are examining the opportunites we have. Strategy depends on which funds are more fruitful and profitable for shareholders," Wong said.
He did not dismiss the possibility of the cash-rich group paying more dividends to its shareholders.
Wong said the group still generated "a positive bottom line" despite vulnerability to rental fluctuations because it leased its retail premises.
Chief executive officer Peter Husum said the company's strategy for Singapore had been to operate small- to medium-size outlets and a larger store or two, and it planned to maintain this strategy.
Similarly for Malaysia, the number of smaller outlets would increase as business grew.
"It is very important that we are bottom line-oriented and not just concentrate on expanding turnover," Husum said.

"We would continue to concentrate on the customer services element and building up our own Robinson's brand and merchandises exclusive to us," he added. "We are focusing on having a clean stock, and target to change the stock level more than four times a year."
Husum said about 70 percent of the group's turnover was generated by local customers, with the remaining 30 percent from foreigners in Singapore and tourists.

Wong was confident the group's ability "to squeeze the highest returns per square foot" under Husum's leadership would protect it amid Singapore's retail slump, which saw its latest victim in Lane Crawford
Hong Kong-based Lane Crawford announced earlier this month it was closing its store in Singapore's prime shopping district.
